original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: On nine pinned R439 D words from four lineages (PR915 helper-free basis, PR926/PR941 pairs, helper triples, PR1062 pair control, three helper-star words), split the literal K_equals_D defect into the part carried by target-to-target reads and the residual left by helper-to-helper gates. Answers PR #4092 open question 2; no replacement contract is adopted.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K implication or a counterexample. Before stating one, the defect it must forgive needs to be located. PR #4092 counted it and r439-k-cross-term-tally identified it with executed-versus-named columns, but neither separated target reads from helper wraps. This split shows what a helper-mixing replacement actually has to cover.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the non-binding bit supplier. The selected complex side and kappa are unchanged. It narrows the defect a helper-wrap replacement for K_equals_D must forgive to the donor sectors, and shows target-read closure alone is unsound once helper gates exist.
stop_rule: Stop after the nine pinned words, the exact split table, the donor-support identity and six controls. Do not adopt a contract, reprice a profile or search for new words.
evidence: Author-checked finite certificate: PR915 residual is 0 of 17,095 literal bits; on the eight helper-mixing words the residual support equals the donor set (192-236 sectors) and 203-251 sectors pass after target-read closure. E = K and helpers restore on all nine. Verifier research/r439-target-closed-k-residual/verify.py. Also corrects PR #4092's statement that the PR3904 pair lies outside the defect set (register/index mix-up).
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a donor-sector contract (K = N* plus donor columns delivered while each restored wrap is open) replace K_equals_D on these words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would be checkable from D alone, would reject the mismatched-K control that K = N* accepts, and would cover exactly the residual this package locates.
open_questions.first_step: State it for well-nested restored wraps and test it on the nine words and the six controls.
open_questions.blocked_by: Adopting it as the H2/K interface is a maintainer policy decision; the finite test has no blocker.

open_questions.question: Does the PR915 semantic substitution proof already cover target-read closure, so the 612 target-to-target reads need no separate H2 repair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Closure removes the K mismatch from target reads but not H2's literal read-kind clause.
open_questions.first_step: Read PR915's PROOF.md substitution argument against the N* definition used here.
